arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Anthony Falzone argued Section 514 took millions of works out of the public domain.
He claimed this unprecedented action violated the Copyright Clause and the First Amendment.
General Verrilli responded by addressing the concept of setting the copyright term at zero.
He argued this approach distinguishes the statute from standard copyright term extensions.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the limits of congressional power over copyright terms. It asks whether the Copyright Clause permits restoring protection to works that previously lacked it.

Justice Sotomayor asked if the lack of initial protection distinguishes these works from standard term extensions.

paragraphs: The outcome defines the scope of public domain rights. It determines whether Congress can retroactively restore copyright to foreign works. This affects access to cultural and historical materials for all Americans.
